title: The canonical quotient sequence compared with the decalage tower
statement: For every abelian category C, the fixed canonical quotient sequence of every filtered cochain complex [lem-sp-filtered-complex-canonical-model] is isomorphic to the E2 sequence of its concrete decalage-tower spectral object [def-sp-filtered-complex-decalage-tower]. These isomorphisms are normalized so that for every filtered map the canonical page-two map, conjugated by the page-two interval comparison, is exactly the induced spectral-object interval cohomology map [lem-sp-spectral-object-page-two-functor]. No boundedness or CE hypothesis is required.

source.document: Stacks Project, Homological Algebra and Derived Categories
source.place: Tag 012K, cycle/boundary formulas for filtered-complex spectral sequences; Tag 015X, Remark 13.26.15, the second filtration.

proof.text: Use the proved cone-to-cokernel quasi-isomorphism for every finite interval. Its naturality identifies interval maps with the maps on quotients of decalage steps.

Write Z_s(F)^(p,n) = F^p K^n intersect d^-1 F^(p+s) K^(n+1). The E_s denominator is Z_(s-1)(F)^(p+1,n) plus d Z_(s-1)(F)^(p-s+1,n-1). For a=p-n and r>=2, substitution in the decalage formula and d squared equal to zero give Z_(r-1)(Dec F)^(a,n)=Z_r(F)^(p,n), and the two denominator terms agree respectively. Thus E_(r-1)(Dec F)^(a,n-a) equals E_r(F)^(p,n-p). With tower index q corresponding to Dec(F)^(1-q), the spectral-object page at (p,q) is the original quotient cycle/boundary page at (p,q), starting at page two.

The comparison sends representatives to their own quotient classes. The differential is represented by d on both sides, and the successor homology comparison is the same quotient map. Cancel the epic representative maps to prove compatibility and assemble an isomorphism of entire sequences.

For a filtered map, restrict to the representative pullbacks and descend to the boundary quotients. Cancellation gives the stated normalized page-two naturality. Infinite endpoints are the zero and full complexes; finite-page calculations use finite endpoints only.

lean.statement:
theorem filteredComplex_decalage_comparison
    (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] :
    ∃ e : ∀ U : FilteredObject (CochainComplex C ℤ),
      (filteredComplexCanonicalModel C).S.obj U ≅
        ((filteredComplexDecalageSpectralObjectFunctor C).obj U).E₂SpectralSequence,
      ∀ {U V : FilteredObject (CochainComplex C ℤ)} (t : U ⟶ V) (p q : ℤ),
        (((filteredComplexCanonicalModel C).S.map t).hom 2).f (p, q) ≫
            (Abelian.SpectralObject.pageTwoComparison
              ((filteredComplexDecalageSpectralObjectFunctor C).obj V)
              (e V) p q (p + q) rfl).hom =
          (Abelian.SpectralObject.pageTwoComparison
            ((filteredComplexDecalageSpectralObjectFunctor C).obj U)
            (e U) p q (p + q) rfl).hom ≫
            (((filteredComplexDecalageSpectralObjectFunctor C).map t).hom (p + q)).app
              (ComposableArrows.mk₁
                (homOfLE (by simp : (q : EInt) ≤ ((q + 1 : ℤ) : EInt))))
